# Independent review: BGM Humanize It candidate package

Scope: the six files under `skill/bgm-humanize-it` checked against `outputs/BGM-Humanize-It-Creation-Prompt.md`. No earlier reviews were read. No web/MCP/source access was used — research-claim findings below assess the wording's internal discipline only, not the cited sources themselves.

## Completeness (P1–P11 against the six files)
No material findings. Structure matches P3 exactly (`SKILL.md`, `agents/openai.yaml`, three references, `LICENSE`), no extraneous files. Frontmatter and `interface` block reproduce the prompt's required YAML verbatim (SKILL.md:1-4; agents/openai.yaml:1-4). SKILL.md body is ~766 words, inside the "roughly 500–800" aim. All nine P3-mandated entrypoint elements (purpose, trigger boundaries, intake, priority order, source/sample and fiction/nonfiction safeguards, workflow, output behaviour, final reread, conditional reference links) are present.

## Source and sample separation
No material findings. SKILL.md:14 and editing-and-voice.md's Samples section both state sample-only facts/phrases aren't draft material without authorisation, and overlap with a sample neither requires deleting legitimate draft wording nor proves authorship — matching P4 closely.

## Citation and factual fidelity
No material findings. SKILL.md:20 and editing-and-voice.md's "Meaning and evidence" section require citations to stay matched to the claims they support, transparent correction rather than silent guessing, and explicitly carry the V2 six-of-twelve/75% worked example — demonstrating, not just asserting, the fidelity rule.

## Fiction boundaries — Low severity
The explicit prohibition on presenting invented/fictional material as real nonfiction evidence ("Do not present invented evidence or real-person experience as nonfiction," P5.4) appears only in genres.md's Creative and lyrical section (genres.md:15), not in SKILL.md. P3 asks for "nonfiction/fiction safeguards" to sit in the entrypoint "so they apply even when no reference is loaded." SKILL.md:22 states the fiction *permission* ("Explicit fiction may invent scenes, speakers, dialogue and imagery... without factual citations") but not this reverse constraint.
Counterexample: a request to "add a short fictional vignette dramatising the client's day" embedded inside an otherwise nonfiction brief may not trigger loading genres.md, leaving only the nonfiction-fabrication ban (SKILL.md:22, first sentence) to *imply*, not state, that the vignette must not be passed off as a real account.
Correction: append one clause to SKILL.md:22, e.g. "Do not present invented fiction as real evidence or attribute it to a real person."

## Voice and genre rigidity
No material findings. Each genre entry preserves the "do not impose" counterpart from P7 (e.g., genres.md Academic: "Do not force contractions, casual substitutions, fragments or categorical claims"), and none of the five sections introduces a new mandatory rule beyond what the prompt licensed.

## Output and Desk format
No material findings. The Teamwork Desk rules (genres.md:21-23) reproduce P7's HTML-by-default, supplied-first-name, no-invented-name, no-send, and "doesn't turn every email into HTML or prohibit sign-offs elsewhere" safeguards without adding rigidity. Finished-text-only default with honoured exceptions (SKILL.md:40) matches P7.

## Unsupported research claims and detector mechanisms — informational / verification boundary
No wording-discipline defects found. research.md separates empirical evidence, editorial convention, house preference and hypothesis (research.md:5-9), labels its own typography conclusion as "Our inference" rather than attributing it to the Microsoft source (research.md:29), and marks all three video leads as inaccessible ("returned internal errors on 14 October 2026... No transcript... is included," research.md:46) and seven further leads as "not inspected... no assertion... is adopted" (research.md:52-60) — consistent with P8's "omit the claim and state the access limit" rule.
Boundary: with no source/web access in this review, I can confirm only that the stated wording is internally disciplined (categorised, limited, hedged) — not that the Wang et al. or Dugan et al. paraphrases match the cited papers, or that the Microsoft URL is current. That remains unverifiable from this review alone.
Detector mechanisms — Low severity: all major P6/P8 rejected techniques (detector scores, self-rewrite similarity, synonym tricks, homoglyphs, watermark removal, decoding recipes) are explicitly rejected (SKILL.md:34; editing-and-voice.md:41). Three specifically named P6 techniques — "artificial lowercase," "arbitrary asymmetry," "disfluency quotas" — aren't restated by name anywhere; they're only generically covered by "Do not inject errors, forced loose ends, slang..." (SKILL.md:34) and "Do not manufacture deliberate misfires, mistakes, poor links... fake self-corrections or forced unresolved endings" (editing-and-voice.md:41). Practical risk is low, since SKILL.md:34's "Redirect detector-evasion requests to useful editing without score promises or authorship verdicts" already catches a user framing any of the three as detector evasion. Correction (optional): add "forced lowercase, artificial asymmetry or disfluency quotas" to the SKILL.md:34 or editing-and-voice.md:41 list for named coverage.

## Discovery metadata
No material findings in the files themselves. agents/openai.yaml reproduces the required `interface` block exactly, including `$bgm-humanize-it` inside `default_prompt`. The frontmatter description (SKILL.md:3) adds the explicitly-permitted discriminating sentence about code/research/translation/formatting/typo-only tasks not needing a rewrite, matching P3's "keep discovery discriminating" instruction. Confirmation against the live skill schema (short_description limit, supported fields) requires the installed skill-creator/validator, which is outside this file-based review's access — a P9 validation step, not a defect in the candidate text.

## Test gaps
P9's forward-testing (V1–V20) and P10's adversarial/Claude construction reviews are process artefacts outside the six package files; per the task's scope, I did not open the existing review or evidence files in `outputs/skill-build-evidence/`. The instructional text is internally consistent with the V1–V20 targets (e.g., V2's correction-transparency has a worked example in editing-and-voice.md; V13's embedded-instruction resistance is stated in SKILL.md:14; V15's Desk/team dual-register case is covered by genres.md), but textual consistency is not demonstrated behaviour. Confirm actual pass/fail status from the evidence directory before treating any invariant as satisfied; this review cannot substitute for that.

## Overall
No High or Critical findings. Two Low-severity completeness nuances (fiction-boundary statement placement in the entrypoint; three P6 techniques not named verbatim), both with low practical risk given overlapping general safeguards elsewhere in the same files, plus clearly bounded verification/test gaps that require source access or execution outside this review's remit.
